title: The Podcast: Release Me From This Demon

illustration.alt: Mary Childs speaks into a podcast microphone as a worried prime-broker worker catches a heavy bag labeled “Hedge-Fund Oopsie,” with a flat waffle nearby.

elementaryChecklist.financialMechanism: Prime brokers provide financing and other services to hedge funds, and can be left with losses when a hedge-fund client cannot meet its obligations.
elementaryChecklist.centralJoke: When hedge funds have “oopsies,” the prime broker may be left literally “holding the bag.”

preschool.title: Mary Childs and the Hedge-Fund Oopsies
preschool.lesson: Prime brokers finance and service hedge funds; if a fund cannot meet its obligations, the prime broker may be left absorbing the losses—holding the bag after the fund’s “oopsie.”
paragraphs:
A fresh Money Stuff podcast was ready to play;
Mary Childs joined as guest co-host for the day.
From Mary in America, she took to the mic,
For markets and oddities, bets and the like.

Sports betting met swap rules. A swap, if you please,
Trades payments between two parties who agree.
They covered mention markets and waffles gone flat,
And brokerage accounts where folks gamble on that.

Then prime brokerage entered: these brokers provide
Hedge funds with financing and services beside.
But when a fund has an “oopsie” and cannot repay,
The broker may hold the bag at the end of the day.

They discussed relationship businesses, banking made narrow,
And why hand-wringing needn’t fill every tomorrow.
Martin Shkreli’s comeuppances entered the mix,
Then short-selling metaphysics brought puzzling tricks.

The episode waits on Spotify and Apple today,
With Bloomberg’s Money Stuff guiding the way.

What happened? A new episode of Money Stuff: The Podcast featured guest co-host Mary Childs and covered betting, swaps, prime brokerage, hedge-fund losses, Martin Shkreli, short selling, and other topics. Prime brokers can suffer losses when hedge-fund clients fail to pay what they owe.
